newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lebanon monitoring group to meet on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon monitoring group to meet on Thursday.

text.p: An international monitoring group will meet on Thursday to discuss a flare-up of fighting in southern Lebanon, the French Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday.
Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux, urging the warring sides to exercise restraint, said the group of Lebanese, Israeli, Syrian, U.S. and French officials would meet in Naqura, Lebanon.
"Lebanon, which is in the process of rebuilding itself, must not become a battlefield," Doutriaux said.
"We urge the utmost restraint on all parties," he added, saying civilians were the innocent victims of the conflict.

Seven civilians were killed when pro-Israeli militia shelled the southern Lebanese port of Sidon on Monday in retaliation for a bomb attack on a car. Scores of Katyusha rockets fired from Lebanon slammed into northern Israel early on Tuesday, wounding at least one civilian.
The monitoring group was set up in April 1996 under a U.S.-brokered accord, after major fighting in southern Lebanon between Israeli forces and guerrillas of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah organization.
